transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, doctor... I'm here because I've been having these nights where I just eat and eat. And afterward, I just sit there with all the crumbs and empty containers around me. I feel so ashamed and... just disgusted with myself. It gets so bad that the next morning, I can hardly even bring myself to pray, let alone look folks at church in the eye. I just can't keep living like this.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don't. I've never done that. I just... I just sit there feeling miserably full. But I don't ever try to make myself throw up or anything like that.
When those eating episodes happen, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?

Yes, that's exactly what happens. It's like... once I take that first bite, usually after the house gets quiet for the night, my good sense just steps aside. I'll be sitting there, actually telling myself in my head, "Belinda, stop now," but... my hands just keep reaching for more. I just can't seem to make myself stop, no matter how much I want to.
After these eating episodes, do you do anything to try to make up for them, like taking laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't take laxatives or pills, and at my age, I'm certainly not out exercising a whole lot. I just... I just wake up the next day feeling awful about it, but I don't do anything to try and make up for the eating.
How often do these eating episodes happen?
Well, since my friend passed away, these late-night eating spells have been happening at least once or twice most weeks. And, honestly, there hasn't been a month where they've really let up at all.
During these episodes, do you eat an unusually large amount of food compared with what most people would eat in a similar period of time?

Yes, it's a lot. On a bad night, I'll start with a plate of leftover casserole from a funeral luncheon, and... well, before I know it, I've eaten all of that, plus half a pan of brownies, some biscuits, and whatever chicken salad is left in the fridge. And that's all just sitting there at the table at one time. I know it's much more than anyone else would eat.
How much does your body weight or shape affect how you feel about yourself?

I don't really think it affects me all that much, to be honest. I mean, at my age, I'm not exactly worried about having a perfect figure anymore. 

It's not really about how I look. I... I feel terrible about the eating itself, and losing control like that, but my weight or my shape doesn't really change how I feel about who I am as a person. I just haven't really focused on that part of it.
